body.statement:
Every capped clipped-ramp member lies in Li and Zhao's baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class and fails the negligible-increment requirement in their Gaussian Condition 3(ii). Therefore every sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets that is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over that baseline class inherits, for every \(0<d<d_{\max}\) and each sign of the corresponding clipped-ramp pair,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
Only this converse transfers by subclass inclusion. Neither the exact two-sign attaining rule nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem is asserted on Li and Zhao's larger class.
body.proof_tex:
The sourced baseline-class lemma records the requirements relevant here. In the constant-intensity clipped-ramp construction,
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,c/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
These probabilities are deterministic functions of every history, strictly between zero and one, and sum to one. The established membership proposition supplies fixed bounded potential outcomes and predictable zero regression. Thus every such array lies in Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.

We verify failure of the negligible-increment condition. Put
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\},
 \qquad
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization yields
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
Distinct increments are orthogonal by iterated conditioning. Once \(n\) is large, the cap is inactive whenever \(g(t/n)>0\). Therefore, if \(W_n\) is the variance of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error,
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^ng(t/n)^2(t/c-1),
 \qquad
 \frac{W_n}{n}\longrightarrow
 w_\star:=\frac1c\int_{a_\star}^1u g(u)^2\,du>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), the outcome envelope is at least \(g(1)>0\), the regression envelope is zero, and the smaller binary assignment probability is \(c/n\) for large \(n\). Hence the scalar negligible-maximum ratio from the sourced Condition 3(ii) satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}
 \max_{1\le t\le n}\frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \ge\frac{g(1)^2}{c^2w_\star}>0.
\]
It cannot be \(o(1)\), proving the stated failure. At the unprojected two-arm level, the identically zero control contribution also produces a zero control row and column, consistent with the same Gaussian obstruction.

Now let the confidence sets be uniformly asymptotically honest over Li and Zhao's baseline class. The inclusion just proved gives, for the selected constant-intensity pair,
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha.
\]
We do not invoke the structured-class premise of the optimized theorem. Instead, use directly the constant-pair finite common-subprobability inequality:
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
At start \(a(d)=1-x(d)\), the sharp theorem gives \(\Delta_n\ge d\) and \(\eta_n\to a(d)^c\). Therefore
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
This direct argument constructs no procedure over the baseline class and consequently transfers neither the pair-specific attaining rule nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem.
body.justification: Every-\(n\) inclusion in Li and Zhao's baseline binary class turns baseline uniform honesty into pair honesty for the constant-intensity witness, after which the finite common-void inequality gives the converse directly.
body.gap: The transfer must not invoke the structured-class premise of the retained frontier theorem; it instead uses baseline inclusion, direct pair honesty, and the constant-pair void-product limit.
body.consumer: Readers may use the constant-intensity lower envelope against baseline-class honesty claims, but not as a positive or globally attained result on that class.
